newsitem.title: USA: Protective Life seeks additional acquisitions.
newsitem.headline: Protective Life seeks additional acquisitions.

text.p: Protective Life Corp president John Johns said the company has enough capital to make another acquisition within the next few quarters despite Tuesday's agreement to buy West Coast Life Insurance Co.
"We hope and believe we have enough redundant capital now to do another acquisition or so within the next few quarters," Johns said in a conference call with analysts Wednesday morning.
"We're not out of the hunt. In fact, we have a couple other deals we're looking at very hard," he said.
Johns said the company will continue to target deals in the $10-$60 million range but said the company is open to doing larger deals as well.
Protective Life on Tuesday said it had agreed to acquire West Coast Life from Nationwide Insurance Enterprise for $257 million in cash.
However, West Coast will pay Nationwide a special dividend of about $100 million before the closing.
In addition, several other special items bring the actual transaction price closer to about $100 million, Johns said.
Johns said the deal is not expected to have a material impact on 1997 earnings.
But, he said, the company expects "some degree of accretion" in 1998.
Johns did not dispute analysts' estimates that the deal will contribute about $0.20 a share to earnings in late 1998 or 1999.
But, he said, analysts should not revise their estimates because earnings in those years also could be affected by other possible deals.
The First Call consensus estimate for 1997 is $3.43 a share and $3.92 a share for 1998.
Although the West Coast Life acquisition is about three times larger than the company's previous largest deal, it was the smallest of the recent deals it's considered, Johns said.
"In the last six to nine months, the transactions that have been available to us have been in the larger size range," Johns said.
He said the company has participated in auctions for three companies and "this is the smallest of the three we've looked at."

Although the company prefers to do smaller deals, "if a larger opportunity were to present itself, though, we would certainly raise additional capital if we thought it was an attractive opportunity for shareholders."
"Within the constraints of our ratings, we'd like to do another deal or so in the near future if we find one that's attractive to us," he said.
Protective Life said West Coast Life had statutory earnings of $12 million in 1996 and last year produced about $20 million in new premium sales.
Johns said Protective Life expects to achieve some cost savings, but declined to estimate the amount.
He said Protective Life plans for West Coast Life to continue in business as a marketing subsidiary.
"We think this is going to be a nice addition to Protective Life," Johns said.
